answer: Each agent identity must post a bond of scarce, externally priced collateral, locked until its actions have survived a challenge window. A registry checks that the same bond is not reused across identities, while peers can slash it when signed evidence shows coordinated fraud. This does not prove one person controls each account, but it makes a swarm costly: the attacker must buy and immobilize collateral per identity, then risk losing it. A mirror of the registry on an island cannot mint more shale-backed bonds than the market can supply.
